docs.title: lua-slds · v0.1.1
docs.text:
SLDS = Identity + Lifecycle + Resolution Semantics. This pure Lua library defines short link behavior independently of HTTP, database clients, caches and authorization. Core has zero runtime dependencies and supports Lua 5.1, Lua 5.3 and LuaJIT.

The host assembles Interactor explicitly with Repository and optional CodeGenerator. Generator/Encoder remain adapter components. See the Chinese README for the Chinese introduction.

docs.title: Start with an explicit code
docs.text:
Install the package and bundled adapters with luarocks install lua-slds. These examples use the v0.1.1 API:

local slds = require("slds")
local interactor = slds.new({
    repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository").new(),
})
local link = assert(interactor:create({}, {
    code = "hello", target = "https://example.com/long/path",
}))
local result = assert(interactor:resolve({}, slds.Identity.new(link.namespace, link.code)))
if result.resolvable then print(result.target) end

docs.title: Behavioral boundaries
docs.text:
• Identity is a logically immutable { namespace, code } tuple.
  • Lifecycle stores ACTIVE, DISABLED or terminal DELETED; expires_at <= now derives EXPIRED during resolution.
  • Resolve reports both existence (found) and permission to resolve (resolvable); errors remain separate.
  • Writes apply sparse patches against the latest authoritative state. Deleted identities remain reserved.
  • Metadata and Hook payloads use independent raw-table snapshots. ctx stays shared and should be read-only.
  • Hooks execute synchronously; callback errors are isolated, callback latency is not.
  • Core does not provide caches, external concurrency coordination, HTTP routing, analytics delivery or authorization.

Version 0.1.1 changes public names and Hook signatures relative to 0.1.0. Read the migration guide before updating an integration.

docs.title: Root module
docs.text:
require("slds") exports:

Field Value / module slds.VERSION "0.1.1" slds.new Factory equivalent to Interactor.new slds.Interactor slds.interactor slds.Identity slds.domain.identity slds.ShortLink slds.domain.short_link slds.Lifecycle slds.domain.lifecycle slds.Resolution slds.domain.resolution slds.Errors slds.domain.errors slds.Hooks slds.hooks slds.HookPoint slds.hook_point

There are no flat status/error aliases, Service, or adapter exports. Require adapters explicitly. Factories use dot notation; instance methods use colon notation.

docs.title: slds.new(opts) -> Interactor
docs.text:
Option Required Contract repository yes Table with create/get/update/delete methods code_generator no Table with generate(ctx,input); returns final Code lifecycle no Partial table of is_valid/can_transition/is_resolvable functions clock no Function returning a finite number; defaults to os.time hooks no Hooks-compatible table with before/after; defaults to empty Hooks

Construction checks method types and fills missing Lifecycle predicates with defaults without mutating the host's table. Supply the same effective Lifecycle functions to the authoritative Repository. ctx must be a table; Core passes the same reference through, without interpreting it.

docs.title: interactor:create(ctx,input) -> ShortLink | nil,err
docs.text:
Input field Contract namespace Non-empty string; defaults to "default" only when nil code Optional non-empty string; only nil invokes CodeGenerator target Non-empty string; rejects javascript:, data: and file: schemes after whitespace/case normalization expires_at Optional finite number metadata Optional opaque table, captured as an independent raw-table graph status Must be omitted; Interactor creates ACTIVE

Core does not fetch or fully parse target URLs. Host URL policy may be stricter. Empty/wrong-type Code returns INVALID without generation. Missing Code without CodeGenerator returns INVALID. Generation receives the original ctx and an independent input snapshot. Generated Code must be a non-empty string; Core does not coerce or retry. Repository enforces uniqueness, including deleted identities.

docs.title: interactor:resolve(ctx,identity) -> ResolutionResult | nil,err
docs.text: Captures identity, reads Repository once, then applies Resolution and the injected clock. Repository NOT_FOUND becomes a normal result with found=false,resolvable=false,status=NOT_FOUND; infrastructure errors remain nil,err. Resolution never writes storage.

docs.title: interactor:update(ctx,identity,patch) -> ShortLink | nil,err
docs.text:
Captures identity/patch and calls Repository.update directly, without a preliminary get. Only target/status/expires_at are allowed. Unknown keys, including metadata, return INVALID. Namespace/code patches raise a programming error. Missing record returns NOT_FOUND; terminal records, invalid fields, rejected rules or can_update return INVALID. Unspecified fields remain unchanged.

expires_at=nil means no change. No clearing sentinel is defined; false returns INVALID.

docs.title: interactor:delete(ctx,identity) -> true | nil,err
docs.text: Calls Repository.delete without a preliminary get. Logical deletion validates the latest record, target state and transition, then retains the identity. Repeat deletion returns INVALID; missing identity returns NOT_FOUND.

docs.title: Identity
docs.text:
Identity.new(namespace,code) requires two non-empty strings. Identity.new(code) uses Identity.DEFAULT_NAMESPACE, "default". Shared metatable methods provide value equality and tostring(identity) as namespace:code.

Identity is an ordinary table with logical immutability: callers must not rewrite fields. The string representation is for display; it is not a collision-free storage key. Store the tuple unambiguously, including strings containing NUL.

docs.title: ShortLink
docs.text:
ShortLink.new(data,lifecycle?) -> ShortLink | nil,INVALID accepts namespace/code, target, optional status (defaults ACTIVE), expires_at and metadata. Invalid/missing identity fields or a non-table container are programming errors; invalid target/status/expiration/metadata returns INVALID.

link:with_patch(patch,lifecycle?) -> ShortLink | nil,INVALID creates a new validated entity. Only explicit target/status/expires_at fields are applied; unknown keys are rejected, immutable keys raise an error, and DELETED cannot be updated. Same-status patches do not invoke the transition predicate.

link:is_expired(now) -> boolean requires finite now and compares expires_at <= now.

link:to_table() -> table exports plain data with independent metadata. Construction, patch and export copy raw table graphs, retaining cycles/shared children and table keys without transporting or invoking metadata metatables. Non-table leaves retain their original values; host resource internals are not isolated. There is no ShortLink:is_resolvable method; use Resolution.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Member Meaning ACTIVE / DISABLED / DELETED The only persistent statuses is_valid(status) Default accepts those three statuses can_transition(from,to) Default permits ACTIVE↔DISABLED and ACTIVE/DISABLED→DELETED is_resolvable(status) Default true only for ACTIVE

A partial override provides only the predicates being changed; each must be a pure synchronous function. Rules may restrict allowed states/transitions. Custom resolvability may permit DISABLED, but DELETED is never resolvable and expired records remain denied. Unknown persistent statuses and terminal revival cannot be authorized by an override. No STATUSES array or validate_transition helper is exported.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
Resolution.resolve(link,identity,now,lifecycle?) -> ResolutionResult evaluates, in order: absence → DELETED → lifecycle denial → expiration → success. Resolution.not_found(identity) constructs absence; Resolution.not_resolvable(link,status) and Resolution.resolvable(link) construct result snapshots. The latter helpers construct results only; callers wanting decisions must use resolve.

Field Contract found Whether the identity exists resolvable Whether the host may resolve it now namespace, code Identity target Present only when resolvable status Actual lifecycle status, Resolution.EXPIRED, or Errors.NOT_FOUND expires_at Stored optional expiration

Custom rules permitting DISABLED resolution preserve DISABLED in the result. Expiration is derived at expires_at <= now, never persisted. ResolutionResult is independent of the entity and has the shared Resolution metatable.

docs.title: Errors and dependency responses
docs.text:
Error Expected use Errors.NOT_FOUND Missing Repository identity Errors.CONFLICT Duplicate create or adapter-declared conditional commit conflict Errors.INVALID Invalid business fields, transitions, terminal writes or policy rejection

Expected failures return nil,err, without added prefixes. Infrastructure errors retain their original values. Success returns result,nil; delete success must be true. Dependency nil,nil, result plus non-nil error, wrong record type or wrong delete success type is a programming error. Unexpected exceptions propagate. Programming errors are not guaranteed AFTER callbacks.

docs.title: Hooks and HookPoint
docs.text:
Hooks.new() creates an empty registry. hooks:on(point,fn) is the only registration API; Interactor only dispatches observers. Complete registration during application startup, before operations begin. Changing registrations while operations are running is unsupported; no freeze/lock API is provided. hooks:on(point,fn) appends a callback and returns the registry. Points are BEFORE, AFTER, BEFORE_CREATE/AFTER_CREATE, BEFORE_RESOLVE/AFTER_RESOLVE, BEFORE_UPDATE/AFTER_UPDATE, BEFORE_DELETE/AFTER_DELETE and ON_ERROR. Their values are lower-case strings such as "before_create".

Same-point callbacks execute in FIFO registration order; no priorities or sorting are defined. Order: general BEFORE → specific BEFORE → operation → specific AFTER → general AFTER. Each point preserves registration order. BEFORE follows argument-container/identity checks and input capture, preceding generation and business validation. Every normal return, including INVALID/CONFLICT and infrastructure errors, reaches AFTER.

Point Callback BEFORE_CREATE fn(ctx,point,input) BEFORE_RESOLVE / BEFORE_DELETE fn(ctx,point,identity) BEFORE_UPDATE fn(ctx,point,identity,patch) AFTER_CREATE / AFTER_UPDATE fn(ctx,point,link,err) AFTER_RESOLVE fn(ctx,point,result,err) AFTER_DELETE fn(ctx,point,ok,err) ON_ERROR fn(ctx,failed_point,hook_err)

General observers receive the actual operation point and corresponding arguments. ON_ERROR's second argument is the failed point; its own exceptions are isolated without recursion. Each callback gets independent domain payload snapshots, preserved root domain methods and nil argument positions. ctx is shared, read-only by convention. Callback returns are ignored; pcall isolates exceptions, not latency, mutation of ctx or event durability.

Dispatcher methods hooks:before(ctx,specific_before_point,...) and hooks:after(ctx,specific_after_point,...) reject incorrect points. Hosts normally register observers and let Interactor dispatch.

docs.title: Core ports
docs.text:
require("slds.ports.repository") and require("slds.ports.code_generator") document interfaces; their stub methods raise errors. Implementations use duck typing, with no inheritance requirement.

Method Success / failure repository:create(ctx,link) Independent ShortLink / nil,err; atomic identity uniqueness repository:get(ctx,identity) Independent ShortLink / nil,NOT_FOUND or infrastructure error repository:update(ctx,identity,patch) Updated independent ShortLink / nil,err; latest-state atomic validation/commit repository:delete(ctx,identity) true / nil,err; terminal logical deletion code_generator:generate(ctx,input) Final non-empty string / nil,err

Repository updates validate a complete candidate using the raw sparse patch before calling an optional can_update(current,patch). This authoritative pure, synchronous, non-yielding boolean predicate is injected only into the Repository. False returns INVALID; exception or non-boolean is a programming error and must leave storage unchanged. Its arguments must not affect committed data if mutated. Delete uses the same full entity/transition validation, without calling can_update. Atomicity must be implemented by the actual storage adapter, not by a Core pre-read.

docs.title: Bundled adapters
docs.text:
Module / constructor Scope slds.adapters.inmemory.repository.new({lifecycle?,can_update?}) Nested namespace/code map; independent snapshots; atomic non-yielding methods within one Lua VM slds.adapters.composed.code_generator.new({generator,encoders?}) Inner generate(ctx), then ordered encoder:encode(previous); final Code validation slds.adapters.sequential.generator.new(start?) Exact integer start in [0,9007199254740991], default 1 only for nil; uniqueness only within that instance slds.adapters.base62.encoder.new() Pure deterministic alphabet 0–9,A–Z,a–z; exact integers in [0,9007199254740991]

Composed captures a dense encoder array at construction; holes/non-encoder entries are programming errors. Empty arrays are valid when the inner generator already returns Code. Intermediate values are opaque; only nil means failure. First failure stops the pipeline and passes its error unchanged. Nil,nil or value+error is a programming error. Final empty/non-string output returns INVALID. The input argument is unused by this reference adapter.

Sequential returns the maximum once, then persistently returns nil,"generator exhausted". Invalid starts or unsupported Base62 inputs raise errors. Base62's range does not support full uint64; do not use tonumber to coerce large string IDs. External generators/encoders must agree on representation and range; Repository remains the uniqueness authority. No external Redis/Postgres/cache adapter is bundled.

docs.title: Supply a direct CodeGenerator
docs.text:
Implement one method returning final Code. Use this when the host already has its own identifier service or code algorithm:

local generator = {
    generate = function(self, ctx, input)
        return "campaign-" .. input.metadata.campaign
    end,
}
local slds = require("slds")
local interactor = slds.new({
    repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository").new(),
    code_generator = generator,
})
local link = assert(interactor:create({}, {
    target = "https://example.com", metadata = { campaign = "spring" },
}))

The example intentionally produces a deterministic Code: repeated creation conflicts, rather than becoming an idempotency API. Repository enforces uniqueness. Core passes unchanged ctx and an independent input snapshot. Return nil,err for expected failures; nil,nil is a programming error. Core performs no automatic retry or numeric coercion.

For internal Generator/Encoder composition, use the bundled Composed adapter. Its encoder array is dense and ordered; an empty array is valid if the inner generator already returns Code. The current Base62 accepts only exact integers in [0,2^53-1]; full uint64/string identifiers need a compatible external encoder. Do not coerce them with tonumber.

docs.title: Choose bundled building blocks
docs.text:
InMemory, Sequential, Base62 and Composed are ready to assemble through their documented constructors. InMemory state belongs to its Lua instance/VM and is lost on restart. Sequential counters are instance-local and restart when recreated; independent counters can produce the same ID. Use a host-selected authoritative Repository for durable storage and cross-process uniqueness.

The three executable compositions in spec/composition_spec.lua use unchanged Core ports: Sequential→Base62, URL-derived Code and a three-tier Repository. A URL generator must define collisions and still let Repository return CONFLICT; deterministic generation does not imply idempotency. The tiered test routes all writes through its third tier and invalidates both fronts; external writers, distributed invalidation and cache products require their own integration contracts. No new production adapter is added.

docs.title: Customize Lifecycle and authoritative update policy
docs.text:
Supply the same rules to Interactor and Repository. Missing predicates use defaults; the original table is not modified:

local slds = require("slds")
local Repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository")
local rules = {
    can_transition = function(from, to)
        return slds.Lifecycle.can_transition(from, to)
            and not (from == slds.Lifecycle.DISABLED and to == slds.Lifecycle.ACTIVE)
    end,
}
local repo = Repository.new({
    lifecycle = rules,
    can_update = function(current, patch)
        return patch.target == nil or patch.target == current.target
    end,
})
local interactor = slds.new({ repository = repo, lifecycle = rules })

This example prevents re-enabling a disabled link and prevents changing target. Invalid field values are rejected before can_update executes. The predicate receives the latest entity and raw sparse patch; false returns INVALID, while a thrown error or non-boolean is a programming error. It must be pure, synchronous and non-yielding. It does not run for delete. Its mutation cannot become committed data.

No override can admit an unknown persistent status, revive DELETED, resolve DELETED or bypass expiration. A custom is_resolvable may allow DISABLED, in which case the result retains status DISABLED. The host should use result.resolvable.

docs.title: Implement an authoritative Repository
docs.text:
Provide create/get/update/delete; see exact signatures. No inheritance is needed. On success return an independent ShortLink, except delete returns true. Missing identity returns nil,Errors.NOT_FOUND, never nil,nil. Pass infrastructure errors unchanged.

For update, perform the following inside the adapter's atomic commit mechanism:

  1. Read the latest record and reject missing/DELETED state.
  2. Build a complete candidate using current:with_patch(patch,lifecycle), validating fields, allowed keys and transitions.
  3. Evaluate optional can_update on isolated current/patch observations.
  4. Commit only after all checks succeed, preserving unspecified fields.

Delete must apply full entity and transition validation with status=DELETED before committing. Repeated deletion returns INVALID. Identity uniqueness remains reserved, including after expiration and deletion.

Store { namespace, code } without delimiter collisions; namespace/code can contain NUL. Declare the serializer's supported metadata types: Core's raw cyclic-table snapshots do not imply that JSON or a database can serialize those graphs. Input and returned values must not alias storage.

An external storage adapter needs real transactions, locking, CAS or an equivalent atomic mechanism. Unprotected get/modify/set does not satisfy the contract; Interactor performs no update/delete pre-read. InMemory's guarantee is limited to non-yielding operations within one Lua VM.

docs.title: Conditional commits and caching
docs.text:
can_update rejection is INVALID; it is not automatic stale-read detection. An external adapter may support host-specific opaque ctx conditions and return CONFLICT on a CAS mismatch. Core adds no revision field or conditional-update framework. Test and document that optional capability separately.

A cache decorator implements the same Repository port. It owns invalidation, negative entries, stale refill races and post-commit invalidation failures. Caching entities lets Resolution recompute expiration from the current clock. Core provides no cache implementation or consistency guarantee; cache/real concurrency claims need adapter integration evidence.

docs.title: Register observers
docs.text:
local slds = require("slds")
local hooks = slds.Hooks.new()
hooks:on(slds.HookPoint.AFTER, function(ctx, point, value, err)
    -- Send to the host's bounded telemetry path; handle value=nil on failures.
    print(point, value ~= nil, err)
end)
hooks:on(slds.HookPoint.ON_ERROR, function(ctx, failed_point, hook_err)
    print("Hook failure", failed_point, hook_err)
end)
local interactor = slds.new({
    repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository").new(), hooks = hooks,
})

Finish all hooks:on registrations at application startup, before operations. Changing the registry during dispatch is unsupported. Register multiple functions by repeated on calls or a host loop; no bulk, priority or lifecycle APIs are needed.

General BEFORE runs before operation-specific BEFORE; specific AFTER runs before general AFTER. Registration order applies within each point. Callbacks get the actual operation point and v0.1.1 arguments. All normal returns, including repository/generator errors, reach AFTER. Programming errors may propagate before AFTER.

Each observer receives an independent payload snapshot retaining domain methods and nil gaps. ctx retains its reference and should be read-only. Hooks cannot transform operations. pcall isolates exceptions, not latency; use host-managed delivery for durable or asynchronous events. ON_ERROR failure does not recurse.

docs.title: Resolve in a host
docs.text:
local function resolve_or_fallback(interactor, ctx, identity, fallback_url)
    local result, err = interactor:resolve(ctx, identity)
    if not result then return nil, err end
    if result.resolvable then return result.target end
    return fallback_url
end

The host maps result.resolvable to redirects or application behavior, maps infrastructure errors to its own failure response, and performs authorization before calling Core. Namespace is a logical identity partition, not tenant authorization. ctx propagation alone proves no access isolation.

In OpenResty, construct a worker-local Interactor in the host and acquire connections in a phase supported by the chosen client. Core has no ngx dependency. A Lua Interactor cannot be stored in ngx.shared; cross-worker persistence/uniqueness belongs to the selected adapters.

docs.title: Verify an integration
docs.text: Use a deterministic clock to test expiration just before, at and after the timestamp. Run the reusable conformance suites against fresh real adapter fixtures. Declare which evidence is sequential, deterministically interleaved or actually concurrent. Run the per-file coverage gate from fresh statistics; never substitute aggregate coverage.

docs.title: Migrating from 0.1.0 to 0.1.1
docs.text: Version 0.1.1 consolidates domain fixes and API cleanup. Despite the patch version label, it includes public API changes. The pure Lua, zero-dependency scope and four operations remain.

docs.title: Construction and names
docs.text:
0.1.0 0.1.1 slds.service / Service slds.interactor / slds.Interactor new{repository,generator,encoder} new{repository,code_generator?} Flat slds status/error constants slds.Lifecycle and slds.Errors namespaces Errors.EXPIRED / DISABLED / DELETED Resolution.EXPIRED / Lifecycle.DISABLED / DELETED Core Generator/Encoder ports Adapter components; Core CodeGenerator port Interactor/service use(hook) Startup Hooks:on(point,fn), injected explicitly

Existing Sequential/Base62 composition becomes:

local slds = require("slds")
local repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository").new()
local code_generator = require("slds.adapters.composed.code_generator").new({
    generator = require("slds.adapters.sequential.generator").new(),
    encoders = { require("slds.adapters.base62.encoder").new() },
})
local interactor = slds.new({ repository = repository, code_generator = code_generator })

Omit CodeGenerator when every create supplies Code. Only code==nil invokes generation; empty/wrong-type explicit Code returns INVALID. Generation receives ctx,input and returns final non-empty Code. Core adds no prefixes, numeric coercion or retry. The current Base62 does not support full uint64 by converting a large string to number.

docs.title: Domain and writes
docs.text:
• Use result.resolvable before target. found only indicates existence. Expiration is now expires_at <= now, so equality is expired; it remains derived without a write.
  • Use Resolution.resolve instead of ShortLink:is_resolvable. Lifecycle has is_valid/can_transition/is_resolvable, without STATUSES or validate_transition. Supply the same effective partial rules to Interactor and Repository; DELETED remains a hard terminal guard.
  • Repository owns latest-state atomic update/delete validation; Interactor does not pre-read. Preserve unspecified fields and reject terminal writes. Delete checks target state validity and transition.
  • Stable errors are exactly NOT_FOUND/CONFLICT/INVALID. Invalid transition, terminal update, repeated delete and can_update rejection return nil,INVALID. Actual conditional commit conflicts may return CONFLICT. Infrastructure errors pass unchanged.
  • Missing Repository.get must return nil,NOT_FOUND. nil,nil, simultaneous result/error and wrong success types are programming errors.
  • Unknown patch keys, including metadata, return INVALID. Namespace/code patches remain programming errors. Metadata is captured at creation and retained; no update/deep merge is added.
  • Nil expiration means unchanged; false is INVALID. Clearing expiration is intentionally unsupported.
  • Omit status on create: Interactor creates ACTIVE and rejects explicit status.

docs.title: Observers
docs.text:
Register only with Hooks:on during startup, before operations:

local hooks = slds.Hooks.new()
hooks:on(slds.HookPoint.AFTER_CREATE, function(ctx, point, link, err)
    if link then print(point, link.code) else print(point, err) end
end):on(slds.HookPoint.ON_ERROR, function(ctx, failed_point, hook_err)
    print(failed_point, hook_err)
end)
local observed_interactor = slds.new({ repository = repository, hooks = hooks })

Add point as the second callback argument; AFTER also receives err, and AFTER_DELETE receives ok,err. ON_ERROR receives failed_point,hook_err. BEFORE covers generation/business validation after input capture; every normal return reaches AFTER, including failures. Programming exceptions do not promise AFTER.

Order is general BEFORE → specific BEFORE → operation → specific AFTER → general AFTER, FIFO within each point. Payload snapshots remain independent; ctx stays shared/read-only by convention. Callbacks are synchronous, without timeout or durable delivery. Runtime registry mutation is unsupported; no old registration aliases remain.

See API, RFC-0002 and conformance before changing a custom adapter.

docs.title: lua-slds 0.1.1 架构复查报告
docs.text: 本报告依据当前源码、测试及交付配置校订早期分析，供维护者审查架构边界与发布准备情况。API 的精确签名以 API 参考和 RFC-0002为准；从 0.1.0 升级须阅读迁移说明。

docs.title: 定位决定取舍
docs.text:
SLDS 定义 Identity、Lifecycle 和 Resolution Semantics。核心解决短链身份、状态转换和解析结果的一致性，不承担 HTTP、目标请求、数据库连接、鉴权、租户隔离、缓存协调或遥测投递。核心及随库参考适配器没有外部运行时依赖。

因此，优化应优先修复契约漏洞、数据别名污染和错误分类。没有实际需求时，不引入管理器、容器、事件总线、CQRS 框架、批量接口或新的领域端口。维护成本和每次操作的工作量同样属于设计成本。

docs.title: 当前模块与责任
docs.text:
模块 当前责任与边界 Interactor create、resolve、update、delete 四个操作的编排；显式注入依赖 Identity / ShortLink 身份、字段校验、稀疏补丁和逻辑不可变约定 Lifecycle / Resolution 三个持久状态、终态约束和只读解析；过期由时间派生 Repository 唯一性，以及基于最新记录的原子验证与写入 CodeGenerator（可选） 返回最终非空字符串 Code；显式 Code 不调用生成器 Hooks / HookPoint 启动期注册的同步观察者；固定执行阶段与异常隔离 InMemory 单 Lua VM 内、不让出执行权的参考存储 Composed / Sequential / Base62 适配器内部的生成与编码组合，不扩展 Core 端口

Core 不导入适配器。宿主负责组装 Repository、可选 CodeGenerator，以及一致的 Lifecycle。公共入口是 Interactor；旧 Service、平铺常量和旧 Hook 注册方式已移除。

docs.title: 已收敛的关键契约
docs.text:
• 身份为 namespace/code，公开更新不允许修改。DELETED 为终态，删除身份不可重新创建。
  • update/delete 不在 Interactor 预读。Repository 在最新记录上验证；更新只提交显式字段，避免旧快照覆盖其他写入。完整字段校验先于 can_update；拒绝返回 INVALID。
  • Patch 只支持 target/status/expires_at。metadata 和未知字段返回 INVALID；nil 表示未提供，不支持用 false 清除过期时间，也不引入 metadata 深合并。
  • 解析区分 found 与 resolvable。未找到是正常解析结果；基础设施故障仍为 nil,err。DELETED 优先拒绝，其后检查可解析规则，再按 expires_at <= now 派生 EXPIRED；解析不写存储。
  • Errors 只有 NOT_FOUND、CONFLICT、INVALID。端口的基础设施错误原样传递，编程错误抛出；不把依赖契约错误伪装成领域失败。
  • Hooks:on(point,fn) 是唯一注册入口。阶段固定为通用 BEFORE、操作 BEFORE、操作、操作 AFTER、通用 AFTER；同点回调按注册顺序执行，正常成功及失败都执行 AFTER。回调异常进入非递归 ON_ERROR。
  • Hook 领域参数逐回调形成快照，ctx 原样传递并约定只读。metadata 使用保留循环与共享引用关系的原始表快照；这不等于对 userdata 等外部资源做深度隔离。
  • Sequential 与 Base62 的精确整数域为 [0,2^53-1]。Sequential 唯一性仅属于单个实例，达到最大值后持续报告耗尽；这些限制属于参考适配器，不属于通用端口。

docs.title: 对早期分析的纠正
docs.text:
早期结论或建议 当前判断 Service 依赖 Repository、Generator、Encoder 三个端口 当前是 Interactor 与两个端口；Generator/Encoder 留在适配器内部 AFTER 只观察成功 正常失败同样触发 AFTER，回调须检查 value/err 只有 L1 合规测试 L0–L3 均存在，默认使用真实参考适配器；自定义实现可注入 fixture factory InMemory 的普通 Lua 写入必然不原子 不让出执行权的操作在单 VM 内成立；不能外推到数据库、多个 worker 或分布式缓存 因文件长度拆分 Service 或引入 CQRS 先检查职责与真实缺陷；当前四操作编排不需要额外架构层 引入 metadata 深合并、批量操作、租户端口或分析端口 缺少领域必需性依据，保留宿主扩展边界 高覆盖率足以证明性能、并发或生产可靠性 覆盖率只反映测试执行到的代码；这些结论需要独立场景和测量

原分析中无法由源码和测试支持的赞誉、性能结论及路线图已移除。局部表复制会产生分配，但它保护已明确的数据隔离契约；没有实际剖析证据，不以削弱隔离来宣称性能优化。

docs.title: 验证与证据边界
docs.text:
当前测试基线为 265 个通过断言用例；Lua 5.1、Lua 5.3、LuaJIT 及额外本地 Lua 5.5 运行中，17 个生产 Lua 文件分别达到 100% 行覆盖率。持续门禁仍为每文件至少 95%，包含入口、端口、内部模块及未加载文件。逐文件清单、重现命令和远端检查入口见验证记录。

组合测试覆盖真实 Sequential → Base62、宿主 CodeGenerator、共享 Lifecycle，以及两个读前端加一个权威写入点。它们验证内存模型中的编排与失效行为，不证明 Redis、数据库事务、外部并发、跨进程唯一性或真实分布式缓存的一致性。pcall 隔离异常，也不意味着 Hook 非阻塞、有超时或可靠投递。

本地 openspec/ 被 Git 忽略；不能把本地提案称为已交付规范。可审查的当前契约保存在版本控制中的 RFC、API、设计决策和迁移说明中。

docs.title: 发布准备与后续改进原则
docs.text:
用户从 LuaRocks 使用 luarocks install lua-slds 安装。发布应先合并通过检查的提交，再对同一提交发布版本标签和 GitHub Release。CI 校验标签与源码版本一致，从该标签生成 rockspec 和源码包，再上传 LuaRocks；发布阶段不自动改写 main。缺少发布密钥或上传失败必须让任务失败。具体步骤见贡献指南的发布说明。

后续只在具体缺陷或宿主集成需求出现时增加实现：外部 Repository 先通过现有合规套件，再补充其事务与并发证据；性能优化先测量，再保持契约进行局部改动。当前没有理由增加 Core 依赖、端口或通用框架。

docs.title: Quick start tutorial · v0.1.1
docs.text: Build a complete short link lifecycle using the bundled reference adapters. No server or database is needed. Examples use the v0.1.1 API.

docs.title: 1. Install the package
docs.text:
luarocks install lua-slds

The package includes the reference adapters under their documented module names.

docs.title: 2. Assemble the two ports
docs.text:
local slds = require("slds")
local Repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository")
local Composed = require("slds.adapters.composed.code_generator")
local Sequential = require("slds.adapters.sequential.generator")
local Base62 = require("slds.adapters.base62.encoder")

local observed, hooks = {}, slds.Hooks.new()
hooks:on(slds.HookPoint.AFTER_RESOLVE, function(_, point, value, err)
    observed[#observed + 1] = { point = point, status = value and value.status, err = err }
end):on(slds.HookPoint.ON_ERROR, function(_, failed_point, hook_err)
    print("Observer failed:", failed_point, hook_err)
end)
local lifecycle = slds.Lifecycle
local repository = Repository.new({ lifecycle = lifecycle })
local now = 1000000
local interactor = slds.new({
    repository = repository, lifecycle = lifecycle, hooks = hooks,
    code_generator = Composed.new({
        generator = Sequential.new(),
        encoders = { Base62.new() },
    }),
    clock = function() return now end,
})

Repository persists entities. CodeGenerator returns final Code; this adapter composes an instance-local counter with Base62. Core never imports either component. If all callers supply explicit codes, omit code_generator entirely.

docs.title: 3. Create
docs.text:
local ctx = {}
local generated = assert(interactor:create(ctx, { target = "https://example.com/long/path" }))
print(generated.namespace, generated.code, generated.status) -- default, 1, ACTIVE

local link = assert(interactor:create(ctx, {
    code = "welcome",
    target = "https://example.com/welcome",
    expires_at = now + 60,
    metadata = { campaign = "launch" },
}))
local identity = slds.Identity.new(link.namespace, link.code)

Namespace defaults only when omitted. Explicit Code must be a non-empty string. Omitted Code invokes the generator; invalid Code does not. New links are ACTIVE, so omit status. Target validation rejects empty values and the javascript:, data: and file: schemes; the host supplies any stricter URL policy.

docs.title: 4. Resolve and expire
docs.text:
local result = assert(interactor:resolve(ctx, identity))
assert(result.found and result.resolvable)
assert(result.target == "https://example.com/welcome")

now = now + 60
local expired = assert(interactor:resolve(ctx, identity))
assert(expired.found and not expired.resolvable)
assert(expired.status == slds.Resolution.EXPIRED)
assert(expired.target == nil)

Equality is already expired: expires_at <= now. The stored lifecycle remains ACTIVE. Always test result.resolvable before using target; result.found alone says only that the identity exists.

docs.title: 5. Update
docs.text:
assert(interactor:update(ctx, identity, {
    target = "https://example.com/new", expires_at = now + 3600,
}))
assert(interactor:update(ctx, identity, { status = slds.Lifecycle.DISABLED }))
assert(not assert(interactor:resolve(ctx, identity)).resolvable)
assert(interactor:update(ctx, identity, { status = slds.Lifecycle.ACTIVE }))

Only target/status/expires_at may be patched. Namespace/code are immutable; metadata and unknown patch fields return INVALID. Nil expiration means unchanged; there is no clearing sentinel. Repository validates and applies the sparse patch against the latest state, preserving unspecified fields.

docs.title: 6. Observe operations
docs.text:
-- Observers were registered before operations in step 2.
assert(interactor:resolve(ctx, identity))
assert(observed[#observed].point == slds.HookPoint.AFTER_RESOLVE)

Register only with hooks:on(point,fn) during startup. Do not change registrations while serving operations. Within one point, callbacks execute in registration order; phase order remains fixed. Each callback receives its own domain payload snapshot. ctx stays shared and should be treated as read-only. Observers execute synchronously; exceptions are isolated with pcall, while callback latency remains part of operation latency. AFTER also receives normal failures, so check value before accessing its fields.

docs.title: 7. Delete and handle failures
docs.text:
assert(interactor:delete(ctx, identity))
local deleted = assert(interactor:resolve(ctx, identity))
assert(deleted.found and not deleted.resolvable)
assert(deleted.status == slds.Lifecycle.DELETED)

local again, err = interactor:delete(ctx, identity)
assert(again == nil and err == slds.Errors.INVALID)
local duplicate, conflict = interactor:create(ctx, { code = "welcome", target = "https://example.com" })
assert(duplicate == nil and conflict == slds.Errors.CONFLICT)

DELETED is terminal and reserves the identity. Expected failures use nil,err; unknown programming failures raise errors. A missing identity resolves normally to found=false/resolvable=false/status=NOT_FOUND, whereas a Repository connection failure returns nil and its original error.

Continue with the operations guide, API reference or v0.1.1 migration guide.

docs.title: Validation for 0.1.1
docs.text: This document records the local verification of the consolidated 0.1.1 source tree and the ongoing gates. It replaces intermediate implementation journals; final remote results belong to the commit checks linked from the release PR.

docs.title: Runtime matrix
docs.text:
Each run starts with fresh LuaCov statistics and independently enforces the same per-file gate.

Runtime Tests Production coverage Lua 5.1.5 265 passed; 0 failures/errors/pending All 17 files: 100% Lua 5.3.6 265 passed; 0 failures/errors/pending All 17 files: 100% LuaJIT 2.1.1784360928 265 passed; 0 failures/errors/pending All 17 files: 100% Lua 5.5.0 (additional local check) 265 passed; 0 failures/errors/pending All 17 files: 100%

The mandatory CI matrix remains Lua 5.1, Lua 5.3 and LuaJIT. A local pass on another runtime does not substitute for a missing supported-runtime result.

docs.title: Per-file coverage
docs.text:
The following modules each reach 100% in every local matrix run; the required minimum stays 95%. Entry points, ports, internal helpers and unloaded production files are included. Coverage cannot be satisfied through aggregate totals, ignored lines, exclusions or stale data.

Production file Each runtime adapters/base62/encoder.lua 100% adapters/composed/code_generator.lua 100% adapters/inmemory/repository.lua 100% adapters/sequential/generator.lua 100% src/slds/domain/errors.lua 100% src/slds/domain/identity.lua 100% src/slds/domain/lifecycle.lua 100% src/slds/domain/resolution.lua 100% src/slds/domain/short_link.lua 100% src/slds/hook_point.lua 100% src/slds/hooks.lua 100% src/slds/init.lua 100% src/slds/interactor.lua 100% src/slds/internal/lifecycle.lua 100% src/slds/internal/snapshot.lua 100% src/slds/ports/code_generator.lua 100% src/slds/ports/repository.lua 100%

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
sh scripts/test.sh
luacheck src/ adapters/ spec/ scripts/check-coverage.lua
luarocks lint lua-slds-scm-1.rockspec
bash scripts/version-manager.sh check 0.1.1
mkdocs build --strict

SLDS_LUA and SLDS_BUSTED may select matching interpreter/toolchains. scripts/test.sh locates the repository relative to itself and removes old coverage files before Busted/reporting/raw-ratio checks. Run the version manager from any working directory; repeated sync to the current version is idempotent.

Additional verification covers installed-package CRUD, all Lua examples from both READMEs and the tutorial, the reusable conformance factory example, rockspec module registration, workflow lint and strict documentation construction from the actual tracked delivery tree. Luacheck checks 45 Lua files with zero warnings/errors.

docs.title: CI and release review
docs.text:
Pushes to main/master and feature-* run CI; pull requests target main/master. Documentation builds on the feature branch and PR, with Pages deployment restricted to main/master. CI installs tools through Actions/PATH, without developer-machine paths. Every supported runtime enforces the per-file minimum before uploading its LuaCov report; upload failure fails the job. Codecov project/patch thresholds are 95%, with zero tolerance.

Release publishing starts when a maintainer publishes a stable GitHub Release. A manual retry requires its explicit published tag. The workflow checks ancestry on main and exact source version, generates/lints the tagged rockspec, attaches matching assets, and uploads using LUAROCKS_API_KEY in the deploy environment. It does not synchronize or commit source during publication. A missing key or failed upload fails the job.

Local shell checks execute the workflow run blocks with controlled gh/luarocks substitutes: valid/invalid tags, draft/missing releases, first publication, exact-version numeric revision selection, search failure, rockspec source mapping and lint failure, missing/whitespace credentials, and upload success/failure. These checks do not publish a release or package and do not prove that the remote secret or environment approval is configured. A real publication result must be checked after the maintainer publishes the Release.

Use the Actions checks for feature-v0.1.1 and the final PR to inspect exact-commit CI and Codecov evidence. A local result or an old implementation commit is not evidence for a different remote revision.

docs.title: Evidence boundaries
docs.text:
• InMemory atomicity is limited to non-yielding operations in one Lua VM. Sequential/interleaving tests do not establish external database concurrency, cross-process uniqueness or CAS correctness.
  • Three-tier composition tests route all writes through a single in-process authority and clear two front tiers. They do not establish distributed invalidation, external writer coordination or negative caching.
  • ctx passthrough does not prove authorization or tenant isolation. The host must test these integrations separately.
  • Hooks are synchronous observers: pcall isolates exceptions, not latency, ctx mutation, sandboxing or durable delivery. Metadata snapshots do not isolate internals of non-table resources.
  • Raw metadata graphs support cycles/shared children without implying an external serializer can store the same graphs. Metadata updates and expiration clearing remain unsupported.
  • Local OpenSpec files remain Git-ignored; tracked RFC/API/migration documents carry the reviewable current contract. The tracked architecture review in report.md reflects the current implementation.

docs.title: Architecture decisions
docs.text: These decisions describe the current 0.1.1 implementation. RFC-0002 defines requirements; migration notes explain changes from 0.1.0. Superseded drafts remain in Git history.

docs.title: Pure domain and explicit composition
docs.text:
SLDS defines Identity, Lifecycle and Resolution semantics using portable Lua and zero runtime dependencies. The host owns HTTP, authorization, tenant policy, storage connections, caches and telemetry delivery. Interactor orchestrates four use cases with Repository and optional final-code CodeGenerator, without discovering adapters or dependencies through ctx.

Generator and Encoder are adapter components, combined by the bundled Composed adapter where useful. Numeric domains and alphabets do not constrain Core. A direct host CodeGenerator needs no internal ID pipeline.

docs.title: Identity, uniqueness and deletion
docs.text: Identity is an ordinary table representing namespace/code, logically immutable by contract. Storage uses unambiguous tuples, including NUL-containing strings. Repository atomically enforces uniqueness; logical deletion reserves identity and cannot be reversed.

docs.title: Derived resolution
docs.text: Resolution returns a separate found/resolvable result. EXPIRED is derived at expires_at <= now and never persisted. The host decides whether to use target from resolvable, not found or a status comparison. No background expiry job or target request is needed.

docs.title: Authoritative sparse writes
docs.text:
Interactor does not pre-read for update/delete. Repository validates against its latest record and commits only supplied fields atomically. Complete validation precedes its optional synchronous can_update predicate; rejection returns INVALID, while an actual adapter CAS conflict may return CONFLICT. Deletes validate both target state and transition. No universal revision field is added.

Partial Lifecycle functions are normalized at construction without mutating host configuration. The host supplies consistent functions to Repository and Interactor. Overrides cannot authorize unknown persistent states or revive/resolve DELETED.

docs.title: Snapshots and errors
docs.text:
Metadata remains opaque, with independent raw-table graph snapshots at ownership boundaries. Table cycles/shared children are supported without transporting metadata metatables. Non-table resources remain host-owned; external serializers may support a narrower set.

Expected failures return nil,err using NOT_FOUND/CONFLICT/INVALID where applicable. Infrastructure errors pass unchanged. Programming errors and malformed result/error pairs raise exceptions; they are not converted by a whole-operation exception wrapper.

docs.title: One observer registration API
docs.text:
Hosts register with Hooks:on(point,fn) at startup, then inject Hooks into Interactor. Dense per-point arrays provide FIFO; general BEFORE, specific BEFORE, operation, specific AFTER, general AFTER define fixed phases. No priority, sorter, plugin lifecycle, bulk registration or freeze API is needed. Runtime registration mutation is unsupported.

Callbacks observe independent payload snapshots. ctx remains shared and read-only by convention. pcall isolates exceptions and ON_ERROR does not recurse, but synchronous callback latency still counts toward operation latency. Reliable or asynchronous event delivery remains outside Core.

docs.title: Evidence instead of broad guarantees
docs.text: Reusable conformance fixtures exercise real reference adapters. In-process sequential/interleaving tests do not prove external database concurrency, distributed cache invalidation or tenant authorization. Every production file must independently meet 95% line coverage from fresh statistics; aggregate coverage cannot substitute. See validation.

docs.title: Design rationale · v0.1.1
docs.text: SLDS answers three questions: which short link is this, which lifecycle changes are valid, and may this link resolve now? A capability belongs in Core only when it is necessary to answer those questions or provide the smallest explicit integration boundary.

docs.title: Ask for the final value
docs.text:
Create needs Code, not an internal counter/UUID and an encoder. Repository and optional CodeGenerator are therefore the only Core ports. Adapter authors can compose generator/encoder components without making every caller configure them. Explicit-code creation works with Repository alone. No new algorithm, registry or generic pipeline framework is needed.

Sequential/Base62 remain useful reference components. Their numeric limits are documented at the adapter level, leaving Core free to accept a non-empty string of any representation or length supported by the host.

docs.title: Validate where the latest state exists
docs.text:
A Core pre-read cannot establish the state present when a database write commits. Interactor.update/delete therefore call the write port directly. Repository applies the same domain value/transition rules to its latest record under an atomic commit mechanism. Sparse patches preserve unrelated concurrent changes; failed validation cannot partially write or revive DELETED.

can_update is a small repository-local business predicate, not a policy engine or automatic stale-read detector. Complete field validation runs first, so invalid expiration values cannot turn an ordinary comparison into an accidental programming exception. Optional CAS remains an adapter/host contract with separate concurrency evidence.

docs.title: Keep time derived
docs.text:
Only ACTIVE, DISABLED and DELETED are stored. Expiration is computed at resolution time using expires_at <= now. Persisting EXPIRED would require scheduled state transitions and complicate extending expiration. Resolution remains pure and storage-free; Repository.get alone cannot tell a host whether it may redirect now.

found and resolvable answer different questions. A disabled/deleted/expired identity can exist while being unresolvable. Custom rules may permit DISABLED, so comparing status to ACTIVE is less reliable than checking resolvable.

docs.title: Extend without weakening invariants
docs.text:
Lifecycle overrides supply three functions, with partial defaults resolved at construction. Hard identity, known-status and terminal guards remain independent of those functions. This allows host-specific restrictions without introducing new status types or a general rule system.

Metadata stays opaque. Raw-table snapshots preserve table ownership without adding serialization, deep merge or freezing. Unknown patches return INVALID rather than silently accepting an operation that had no effect. Expiration clearing is deferred because the latest design requires no sentinel in this version.

docs.title: Observe without controlling the operation
docs.text:
Hooks registers ordered functions by explicit point. General/specific phases make ordering deterministic. BEFORE covers valid calls before generation and business validation; AFTER sees every normal outcome, including failures.

Each observer gets independent domain payloads; ctx remains shared and should be read-only. pcall prevents one observer exception from breaking an operation. It cannot bound callback latency, make delivery durable or protect shared host resources. The host must provide those capabilities if needed.

docs.title: Use Lua conventions and measure claims
docs.text:
Shared class metatables, dot factories, colon methods and explicit construction keep the implementation familiar on Lua 5.1/5.3/LuaJIT. Normalized rules and point-indexed Hook arrays avoid unnecessary work; no I/O pre-read is needed for update/delete. Performance multipliers are not claimed without benchmarks.

Each production file needs fresh independent coverage >=95%; aggregate coverage is insufficient. Real reference adapters power conformance. Sequential tests and controlled interleavings demonstrate defined scenarios, not external database concurrency, cache invalidation or tenant authorization. See validation records and architecture decisions.

docs.title: Domain layer architecture · v0.1.1
docs.text: The domain layer defines identity, lifecycle and resolution behavior with no infrastructure I/O. Interactor coordinates four operations; Repository owns the atomic validation/commit boundary for writes.

docs.title: Objects and responsibilities
docs.text:
Module Responsibility Identity Non-empty namespace/code tuple, logical immutability and value equality ShortLink Validated entity, sparse patches and independent metadata snapshots Lifecycle Three persistent statuses and three default predicates Resolution Pure existence/resolvability/expiration decision and result Errors NOT_FOUND / CONFLICT / INVALID

Identity uses ordinary Lua tables with a shared class metatable. Callers must not assign identity fields. No proxy/freeze framework is introduced. The tuple is distinct from host, URL, tenant or storage key.

ShortLink contains target/status/expires_at/metadata in addition to identity. Only target/status/expires_at can be patched. Unknown fields including metadata return INVALID; immutable identity patches raise an error. Metadata is opaque raw-table data, captured independently across entity/export/storage boundaries. Cycles and alias relationships inside a snapshot survive; metatables do not. Persistence adapters may support a narrower serializable subset.

docs.title: Lifecycle and rules
docs.text:
Persistent statuses are ACTIVE, DISABLED and DELETED. Defaults allow ACTIVE↔DISABLED and ACTIVE/DISABLED→DELETED. DELETED has no outgoing transitions and remains reserved. Same-status patches do not invoke the transition predicate.

Constructors normalize a partial rule table into is_valid/can_transition/is_resolvable defaults without modifying it. A small internal function shares this normalization; it is not a policy manager or new public API. Direct domain calls may use partial rules. Hosts must configure consistent rules in Interactor and Repository.

Custom rules cannot authorize unknown persistent statuses, revival or DELETED resolution. is_valid may restrict states, and can_transition may restrict changes. Custom is_resolvable can permit DISABLED, but expiration and terminal safeguards remain.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
Resolution reads no storage and writes nothing. Repository.get supplies an independent ShortLink; Resolution applies absence, DELETED, custom denial, expiration and success in that order.

ResolutionResult = {
    found, resolvable, namespace, code,
    target?, status, expires_at?
}

Target appears only when resolvable. The actual persistent status survives successful custom resolution. expires_at <= now derives Resolution.EXPIRED without changing the stored entity; no timer or scheduler is needed. NOT_FOUND is a normal absence result, while infrastructure failure remains nil,err.

docs.title: Write authority
docs.text:
The entity defines valid values and transitions. The authoritative Repository must apply those same domain rules to its latest state inside the atomic write boundary. It is responsible for uniqueness, terminal guards, optional can_update and rollback, while Resolution remains responsible for time-dependent read semantics.

Interactor.update/delete do not get first. The repository validates complete candidate fields before can_update; policy observation must not change committed data. Delete also uses full entity/transition validation, including custom validity of DELETED.

docs.title: Lua implementation
docs.text:
Factories use dot notation; instance methods use colon notation; instances share their class metatable. Expected business failures return nil,err, programming errors throw, and only Hook callbacks are exception-isolated. Domain modules depend only on other pure Lua domain/internal helpers. No adapter, ngx, database, JSON or HTTP module is imported.

See RFC-0002, API and ports/adapters.

docs.title: Ports and adapters · v0.1.1
docs.text:
Core requests behavior through two duck-typed contracts. It never imports a concrete adapter. The host explicitly constructs Repository, optional CodeGenerator and Interactor; ctx carries opaque per-call host data, not dependency discovery.

flowchart TD Host --> Interactor Interactor --> Domain[Identity / ShortLink / Lifecycle / Resolution] Interactor --> Hooks[Hooks + HookPoint] Interactor --> Repository Interactor --> CodeGenerator[CodeGenerator optional] InMemory -. implements .-> Repository External[External storage adapter] -. implements .-> Repository Composed -. implements .-> CodeGenerator Composed --> Generator Generator --> Encoders[Ordered Encoder array]

docs.title: Repository
docs.text:
Repository provides create/get/update/delete. Get retrieves an independent entity, leaving read-time resolvability to Resolution. Writes enforce identity uniqueness, latest-state validation, sparse fields and terminal deletion atomically. Failure cannot partially commit. Deleted/expired identities do not become reusable.

Interactor performs no update/delete pre-read. The repository validates a complete candidate, then optional can_update, then commits under the storage's atomic mechanism. can_update=false is INVALID. Delete validates both target-state validity and transition. External storage needs its own transaction/lock/CAS implementation; Core cannot make an unprotected get/modify/set atomic.

The four bundled adapters are ready-to-use general building blocks, not driver stubs. InMemory data is scoped to its object and Lua VM, with no restart durability or cross-worker sharing. The bundled InMemory adapter uses a nested namespace/code map, independent metadata snapshots and non-yielding writes within one Lua VM. It proves neither cross-process uniqueness nor concurrent database behavior. External cache decorators implement the same port and own their consistency model.

docs.title: CodeGenerator
docs.text:
CodeGenerator.generate(ctx,input) returns final Code. Code is the only representation Core needs; it does not need an internal ID, encoder alphabet or numeric domain. Callers supplying explicit valid Code need no generator. Missing Code invokes the optional port; invalid explicit Code is rejected directly.

Composed is a reference adapter, not a new Core framework. It calls generator.generate(ctx), followed by an ordered dense array of encoder.encode(value). Intermediate values remain opaque. Empty encoder arrays work when the generator already returns Code. Failure stops immediately; final output must be a non-empty string.

Sequential and Base62 remain replaceable components inside that adapter. Their exact integer domain [0,2^53-1] and Sequential's instance-local uniqueness/exhaustion do not constrain generic CodeGenerator. Full uint64 or string identifiers need compatible external components without lossy tonumber coercion. Sequential counters are independent per instance and reset when reconstructed; Repository is still the uniqueness authority.

The two ports also support a host CodeGenerator deriving Code from a URL, and a Repository decorator with two read fronts plus one authoritative tier. These are composition choices, not new Core modes. The executable cases in spec/composition_spec.lua cover cold/warm reads, write invalidation, tombstones and failures using in-process storage only; they do not establish external cache consistency or database concurrency.

docs.title: Keep integrations outside Core
docs.text:
Host or adapter concern Why it stays outside Core HTTP/OpenResty Transport does not define identity or resolution Redis/Postgres connections Storage-specific resource and atomicity mechanisms Cache invalidation Adapter-specific consistency and failure model Authorization/tenant policy Namespace and ctx are not access control Telemetry delivery Hook observation does not supply queues or durability CAS/version fields Optional adapter/host condition, not a universal domain value

The API specifies method responses; the operations guide explains integration; conformance defines the evidence an adapter must supply.

docs.title: RFC-0002: SLDS v0.1.1 — Public API and authoritative writes
docs.text:
Field Value Status Current contract for the consolidated 0.1.1 release Version 0.1.1 Date 2026-10-18 Supersedes The 0.1.0 contracts; see the migration guide Runtime Pure Lua 5.1 / Lua 5.3 / LuaJIT

MUST, MUST NOT and SHOULD below describe conformance requirements. API reference gives exact signatures; migration notes list breaking changes. Superseded contracts remain available in Git history.

docs.title: 1. Position and iron rules
docs.text:
SLDS = Identity + Lifecycle + Resolution Semantics. Core remains a small pure Lua library; the host explicitly assembles dependencies. It MUST NOT introduce an HTTP server, database/cache client, JSON library, target request, scheduler, authorization system or durable event framework.

Rule Requirement RULE-001 Core MUST NOT depend on HTTP. RULE-002 Core MUST NOT depend on a specific database. RULE-003 Core MUST NOT fetch Target URLs. RULE-004 Identity namespace/code MUST remain immutable after creation. RULE-005 Repository MUST enforce identity uniqueness atomically. RULE-006 Deleted identities MUST remain reserved by default. RULE-007 Resolution MUST NOT require an external event/analytics system to succeed. RULE-008 Analytics delivery MUST remain outside the resolution critical path. RULE-009 Authorization MUST be implemented by the host. RULE-010 Compatibility claims MUST pass applicable conformance scenarios and declare evidence scope.

Hooks are synchronous observation points. Exception isolation satisfies no latency or telemetry delivery guarantee; the host owns any bounded/asynchronous delivery path needed by RULE-008.

docs.title: 2. API and dependency boundary
docs.text:
Core exposes only four operations through Interactor: create, resolve, update and delete. Root exports VERSION, new, Interactor, Identity, ShortLink, Lifecycle, Resolution, Errors, Hooks and HookPoint. It MUST NOT expose redundant flat status/error aliases or the former Service.

Core's dependency ports are Repository and optional CodeGenerator. Generator/Encoder remain adapter-internal components; numeric ranges, alphabets and ID representations MUST NOT constrain the generic Core port. No port inheritance or dependency container is required. ctx is an opaque table passed unchanged; it is not a dependency locator or authorization mechanism.

Constructors MUST validate injected method/function shapes. Missing Lifecycle predicates MUST be filled using defaults without modifying the host's table. The host MUST configure consistent Lifecycle functions at Interactor and authoritative Repository boundaries.

docs.title: 3. Identity, entity and rules
docs.text:
Identity is the {namespace,code} tuple of non-empty strings. It is logically immutable, represented by an ordinary Lua table with shared class metatable. Callers MUST NOT rewrite identity fields. Storage MUST preserve distinct valid tuples, including NUL-containing strings; a delimiter display string is not sufficient as a storage key.

ShortLink stores identity, target, status, optional expires_at and opaque metadata. Target MUST be a non-empty string and MUST reject javascript:, data: and file: schemes after whitespace/case normalization. Core does not fetch or fully parse the target; host policy may be stricter. Expiration MUST be nil or a finite number. Metadata MUST be nil or a table.

Only ACTIVE, DISABLED and DELETED may be persisted. Lifecycle exposes is_valid, can_transition and is_resolvable. Defaults permit ACTIVE↔DISABLED and ACTIVE/DISABLED→DELETED. Same-status patches do not invoke the transition predicate. Partial overrides may restrict states/transitions or customize resolvability, but MUST NOT admit unknown statuses, revive DELETED or resolve DELETED. Invalid business values/transitions return INVALID.

ShortLink.new(data,rules?) and with_patch(patch,rules?) perform domain validation. The allowed patch fields are target/status/expires_at. Namespace/code patches are programming errors; all other keys, including metadata, return INVALID. Nil expiration means unchanged. v0.1.1 defines no expiration-clearing sentinel; false is INVALID.

Metadata table graphs MUST be independently captured at construction, patch, export, storage and observer boundaries. Preserve graph cycles/shared children/table keys; omit metadata metatables without invoking them. Non-table leaves retain their values; host resource internal state is outside the snapshot guarantee. Adapters may declare a narrower serializable value set and MUST validate it.

docs.title: 4. Resolution
docs.text:
Resolution MUST be a pure domain decision and MUST NOT write Repository. It evaluates:

  1. No record: found=false, resolvable=false, status=NOT_FOUND.
  2. DELETED: found=true, resolvable=false, status=DELETED.
  3. Lifecycle denies resolution: found=true, resolvable=false, actual persistent status.
  4. expires_at <= now: found=true, resolvable=false, status=EXPIRED.
  5. Otherwise: found=true, resolvable=true, actual persistent status and target.

EXPIRED belongs to Resolution.EXPIRED and MUST NOT be persisted. The result includes namespace/code, found, resolvable, status, optional target and expires_at. Target MUST be absent when not resolvable. If custom rules allow DISABLED, a successful result MUST retain DISABLED. Hosts SHOULD decide behavior from resolvable rather than status comparisons.

Repository NOT_FOUND becomes a normal absence result. Infrastructure errors MUST remain distinct nil,err. The injected clock MUST return a finite number.

docs.title: 5. Errors and programming contracts
docs.text:
The stable error set is exactly NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT and INVALID. Expected failures return nil,err; successful values return value,nil. Delete success is true. Infrastructure errors MUST pass unchanged, without prefixes or broad exception conversion.

Missing argument containers, invalid injected methods, identity mutation attempts, malformed port responses and thrown unexpected failures are programming errors. Nil,nil from a dependency and simultaneous result/error are programming errors. A programming exception MAY propagate without AFTER; normal success and failure returns MUST trigger AFTER.

docs.title: 6. Code generation
docs.text:
CodeGenerator.generate(ctx,input) MUST return final non-empty string Code or nil,err. Only input.code==nil invokes it. Explicit invalid/empty Code returns INVALID; missing Code without a generator returns INVALID. Create fixes status to ACTIVE and rejects explicit status. The generator MUST receive independent input and unchanged ctx. Core MUST NOT coerce IDs, retry conflicts or interpret deterministic generation as idempotency.

The reference Composed adapter calls inner generator.generate(ctx), then each encoder.encode(previous) in a captured dense array. Empty arrays are allowed. Intermediate representations remain opaque; only nil signals failure. It MUST stop at first failure, preserve its error, reject malformed response pairs, and validate only the final non-empty string. This does not introduce a Core pipeline framework.

Sequential/Base62 retain exact integer range [0,2^53-1]; Sequential uniqueness is instance-local and exhaustion persists after returning the maximum once. These limits belong to reference adapter contracts. Full uint64/string IDs need separately compatible components.

docs.title: 7. Authoritative Repository
docs.text:
Repository implements create/get/update/delete. Success entities MUST be independent of storage. Create MUST reserve identity atomically, including existing DELETED records. Missing get/update/delete returns NOT_FOUND. Get retrieves an entity without applying Resolution.

Interactor.update/delete MUST NOT pre-read. Repository.update MUST atomically locate the latest record, reject DELETED, validate the complete candidate using the raw sparse patch, evaluate optional can_update, then commit. Invalid fields MUST be rejected before policy evaluation. Unspecified fields MUST remain intact; failure MUST leave storage unchanged.

can_update(current,patch) is an adapter-injected pure synchronous non-yielding boolean predicate, not a Core port. False returns INVALID. Exception or non-boolean return is a programming error with rollback. Its observations MUST NOT alias actual committed data. It MUST NOT run for delete.

Delete MUST validate the complete candidate and current→DELETED transition, including custom is_valid(DELETED). Repeat deletion returns INVALID and MUST NOT erase the identity reservation.

Different-field sparse updates preserve each other; same-field updates follow commit order. This does not promise application stale-read detection. External adapters MAY implement host-specific ctx CAS conditions and return CONFLICT; v0.1.1 adds no generic version fields. Cache decorators MAY implement the same port, with declared consistency and separate tests. Neither external CAS nor caching is bundled or proven by reference tests.

docs.title: 8. Hooks
docs.text:
Hooks stores ordered callback arrays by HookPoint: BEFORE/AFTER, operation-specific before/after points and ON_ERROR. Order MUST be general BEFORE → specific BEFORE → operation → specific AFTER → general AFTER, with registration order within a point.

BEFORE follows programming argument checks and snapshot capture, preceding generation/business validation. Every normal return MUST reach the corresponding specific/general AFTER exactly once. Callbacks use (ctx,point,payload...); AFTER includes value,err and AFTER_DELETE includes ok,err. ON_ERROR uses (ctx,failed_point,hook_err) and MUST NOT recurse on its own failure.

Each callback MUST receive independent domain payload snapshots preserving root domain methods and nil argument positions. ctx MUST retain its original reference and SHOULD be read-only. Callback returns are ignored; each callback exception is isolated with pcall. No timeout, sandbox, asynchronous scheduling or durable delivery is promised. Empty points SHOULD avoid snapshot allocation.

hooks:on(point,fn) MUST be the only registration entry. Interactor MUST only dispatch observers and MUST NOT expose registration methods. Hosts MUST finish registration at application startup before invoking operations. Mutation of registrations during operations is unsupported; implementations MUST NOT add priorities, global sorting or lifecycle/freeze APIs for this iteration.

docs.title: 9. Verification and delivery
docs.text:
All production Lua files under src/ and adapters/ MUST individually reach at least 95% line coverage, including unloaded files, port stubs and internal helpers. Fresh LuaCov measurements MUST run separately on Lua 5.1, Lua 5.3 and LuaJIT. Codecov project/patch targets remain at least 95%, with zero tolerance. Aggregate or merged coverage cannot replace per-file gates.

Reference conformance MUST use actual bundled adapters with fresh fixture factories. Fault injection MAY replace specific methods. Deterministic interleavings MUST NOT be advertised as external concurrency proof, ctx propagation as tenant isolation, or uncached visibility as cache invalidation. Exact interpreter/test/file results and remote status belong in validation records.

Version 0.1.1 consolidates the domain fixes and final Hook API into one reviewed release change. Expiration clearing remains intentionally unsupported, as documented in the migration guide. Local ignored OpenSpec proposals/specs are not part of the Git delivery unless repository policy changes.

docs.title: SLDS conformance tests · v0.1.1
docs.text:
Field Scope Contract RFC-0002 / v0.1.1 source API Default implementation Real InMemory Repository and Composed(Sequential→Base62) CodeGenerator CI interpreters Lua 5.1 / Lua 5.3 / LuaJIT Additional local check Lua 5.5

Compatibility requires the applicable behavioral scenarios plus an explicit evidence declaration. Sequential and deterministically interleaved tests do not establish actual external storage concurrency. Optional cache/tenant/CAS features require separate integration evidence.

docs.title: Reuse the suites
docs.text:
Register the four reusable suites from a Busted spec file. Replace Repository with the actual adapter being evaluated; keep fresh independent fixture state:

local Interactor = require("slds.interactor")
local Repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository")
local Composed = require("slds.adapters.composed.code_generator")
local Generator = require("slds.adapters.sequential.generator")
local Encoder = require("slds.adapters.base62.encoder")

local function make_fixture(opts)
    opts = opts or {}
    local repo = opts.repository or Repository.new({
        lifecycle = opts.lifecycle, can_update = opts.can_update,
    })
    local gen = opts.generator or Generator.new()
    local enc = opts.encoder or Encoder.new()
    local code_generator = opts.code_generator
    if code_generator == nil then
        code_generator = Composed.new({ generator = gen, encoders = { enc } })
    end
    local clock = opts.clock
    if clock == nil then clock = function() return 1000000 end end
    local interactor = Interactor.new({
        repository = repo, code_generator = code_generator,
        lifecycle = opts.lifecycle, clock = clock, hooks = opts.hooks,
    })
    return interactor, repo, code_generator, enc, gen
end

require("spec.conformance.suites.l0_core")(make_fixture)
require("spec.conformance.suites.l1_lifecycle")(make_fixture)
require("spec.conformance.suites.l2_reliability")(make_fixture)
require("spec.conformance.suites.l3_extensions")(make_fixture)

Run from a source checkout with its spec modules on package.path and installed adapter modules available. Each call creates fresh state unless a test explicitly supplies a shared Repository. Keep overrides for fault injection. The third return is now the final CodeGenerator, not the internal Generator.

L2 controlled interleavings wrap the public update method; supply a writable Lua wrapper if your adapter uses userdata. Actual external tests must isolate and clean up records while retaining required identity reservations. The fixture must configure consistent Lifecycle functions at Interactor and Repository.

docs.text:

spec/composition_spec.lua additionally exercises Sequential→Base62, URL-derived Code, explicit shared Lifecycle and a test-only three-tier Repository using real InMemory instances. Its tiered checks cover cold/warm hits, independent snapshots, write invalidation, cached entity expiration, tombstones and failure passthrough. All writes route through one authority; no external cache consistency, distributed invalidation or database concurrency is established. Core and the four bundled adapters remain unchanged.

Additional direct tests cover partial Lifecycle defaults, hard invariants, expires_at==now, unsupported patches, validation before can_update, rollback, full delete validation, no Interactor write pre-read, malformed dependency responses, CodeGenerator pipeline boundaries, full normal-error AFTER paths and nonrecursive ON_ERROR. Reference component numeric limits/exhaustion are tested without imposing their domain on Core.

Relevant files include spec/repository_v02_spec.lua, spec/reference_adapters_spec.lua, spec/value_boundaries_spec.lua, spec/interactor_boundaries_spec.lua, spec/v02_interactor_spec.lua, spec/code_generator_spec.lua, spec/hook_points_spec.lua, spec/hook_observation_spec.lua and spec/public_api_spec.lua.

docs.title: Coverage and declaration
docs.text:
sh scripts/test.sh
luacheck src/ adapters/ spec/ scripts/check-coverage.lua

Each production file under src/ and adapters/ must reach at least 95% from fresh independent statistics, including unloaded files. CI applies the gate separately per interpreter; aggregate/merged coverage is insufficient.

Record contract/suite revision, actual Repository/CodeGenerator components, interpreter, exact commands, applicable extensions, pass/failure counts and unresolved evidence. Label evidence sequential, controlled interleaving or actual external concurrency. Do not turn ctx propagation into a tenant-isolation claim or uncached visibility into a cache-invalidation claim. See validation records.
